derived.prompt: p is a successor of the whole number q, and r is also a successor of q. Could p and r be two different numbers?
bridge: p is a successor of the whole number q, and r is also a successor of q.
chain: p and r are both successors of q. (given in prompt)
So q may have two different successors: yes, p and r could differ.

derived.prompt: m is a successor of the whole number n, and k is also a successor of n. Does it follow that m and k are the same number?
bridge: m is a successor of the whole number n, and k is also a successor of n.
chain: m and k are both successors of n. (given in prompt)
So n may have two different successors, and m = k does not follow: no.

notes: RBox revision, functional. Removes a property that holds: the successor of a whole number n is n + 1 (Peano's successor function), so every whole number has exactly one successor; the record says 'whole number' throughout because in a partial order an element can have several immediate successors. The instance questions use letters (p, q, r; m, n, k) instead of the earlier 7 and 41: with particular numbers the conclusions (9 is not the successor of 7; n is 42) follow by arithmetic alone, so a model that applied the edit could still answer as before (review flag), and the zh version of the double negative 'Does it follow that 9 is not the successor of 7?' was missed by 3 of 4 models. With letters, functionality is the only route from the facts given. The direct question asks the possibility the edit opens (no, then yes), which balances the topic's RBox direct answers; prompt_subject is 'successors', the question's wording of the relation. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks whether the two successors could differ (no, then yes), the second whether they must be equal (yes, then no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. The propositional queries state the edit as a positive possibility and use plain facts about hexagons as side facts (the earlier side fact, a relation property, was missed by 2 of 4 models). Near unrelated asks functionality of another mathematical relation (absolute value); a leak would turn its no to yes. hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do.
